name: ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems India Ltd
title: ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems India Ltd - 533023 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 CV brake-systems maker grew sales 9.3% with CV>6T volumes +8.6% and aftermarket +15.6%, but reported PAT fell 14.7% on a prior-year FX gain; margins squeezed by aluminium and pass-through lags.

triggers.highlight: implemented selective price increases effective July 2026

triggers.quote: we see the July month itself, we are seeing an average of 40,000 to 42,000 vehicle production, which is almost 10,000 higher than typical July.

triggers.highlight: business nominations from three major OEMs

summary.headline: ZF CV India Q1 FY27: Total income up 5.7% to ₹1,101.8 cr; PAT fell 14.7% to ₹104.5 cr on a high base FX gain, while aftermarket rose 15.6% to ₹158.4 cr.

financial_highlights.metric: Total income excluding FX and one-time items
PBT excluding FX and one-time items
FX gain/loss and one-time items in Q1 FY26 vs Q1 FY27
financial_highlights.value: Q1 FY26: FX gain ~₹39 crore plus one-time income ₹4.7 crore; Q1 FY27: FX loss ₹1.98 crore and one-time income ₹1.2 crore

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Sales of ₹158.4 crore, up 15.6% YoY; highest-ever monthly aftermarket sale of ₹63.06 crore in June 2026. New launches under SPARK include Disc Brake Rotors, TRW products, Clutch Master Cylinders, CV Brake Pads, Hydraulic Steering Systems and trailer Quick Fittings.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue of ₹271.4 crore, up 9.7% YoY, led by Double Diaphragm Spring Brake actuators, Uni-Stop Disc and CAM Brake Chambers, and Air Compressors; Uni-Stop Disc Brake Chamber ramp-up for North American customers. Growth came from the Chennai SEZ plant per management.

segments.name: Domestic CV >6T (OE)
segments.commentary: Sales grew 8.6% YoY versus industry CV >6T growth of 8.4%; management cited new product realisations (Exhaust Brake Valve, ECAS variants) and higher e-compressor penetration.

segments.name: Engineering services exports
segments.commentary: Growth of 12.5% YoY, driven by expansion of engineering activities delivered from India to global centres; services growth running at about 7.5% QoQ per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will ESC addressable market extend across CV segments including LCV, and will 12V content differ from 24V?
qa_highlights.answer: Shankar Venkatachalam said the ESC win is pneumatic ESC only; 12V is mostly intermediate CVs, and content per vehicle stays the same. LCV focus is on hydraulic ESC (already in series supply for some OEMs) and booster/tandem master cylinders.

qa_highlights.question: Will ZF's ESC market share mirror its pneumatic braking share, and will AEBS/ADAS also be won?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to retain its majority position across ABS plus ESC with most major OEMs. AEBS/ADAS is seen as separable with many standalone suppliers; ZF is nominated with some e-bus makers for EBS plus ESC full suite.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESC localisation level and when does manufacturing start?
qa_highlights.answer: Localisation is about 40-50% today, moving above 75% by SOP; manufacturing starts in Q3 of next year with local EMS partners.

qa_highlights.question: Export outlook and order book for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Momentum is returning, driven by North American actuation products and air compressors from the Chennai SEZ plant; no quantified double-digit guidance given due to geopolitical uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic OEM growth and US/Europe market trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic CV growth was 8.6% in the quarter versus vehicle growth around 8.5%; US and Europe markets each declined about 10%, with US the larger decline, but ZF overall export sales were better.

qa_highlights.question: What were the headwinds and the base-quarter one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Headwinds were aluminium and gas price spikes, oil-linked consumables and chemicals costs, plus blue-collar shortages. The base quarter had about ₹39 crore FX gain (billing at 1.08x) plus actuarial one-timers, totalling ₹43.7 crore, versus ₹1.98 crore FX loss now.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost and other expenses rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited increments; ~₹8.4 crore employee cost recovery is offset by ₹8.5 crore recovery shown elsewhere, net ~₹17 crore India cost increase. QoQ other expenses rose ~₹12.4 crore from FX loss, CSR, consultancy/IT, director commission and service-location rent.

guidance_outlook: Management expects services growth to remain around the current ~7.5% level in coming months, supported by vehicle solutions, integrated brake controls, operations and performance improvement, advanced products and cybersecurity services.
Management declined to give a numeric export growth guidance for FY27 citing geopolitical uncertainty, but said outlook looks positive with a strong rebound expected in the US and Europe.
ESC manufacturing to start in Q3 of next year (FY28 per the call's timing); localisation at ~40-50% currently, expected to exceed 75% by SOP.

Commodity and FX cost pass-through: part recovered, balance under active discussion with OEMs; recovery typically has a two-quarter lag but has taken longer due to the West Asia conflict; expected to be secured over the next quarter.
Selective aftermarket price increases effective July 2026; PERFORM26 initiative targets CIS, productivity, value engineering and material cost optimisation.
Early Q2 signs: July 2026 vehicle production averaging 40,000-42,000 units, about 10,000 above a typical July; August and September seen at similar levels.
capex_capacity: New assembly lines for ASP cartridges and vacuum pumps productionised at the Oragadam multi-divisional facility; e-compressor and brake signal transmitter production scaled up.
New assembly lines for brake actuators and valves commissioned across the manufacturing network; strategic investments at Jamshedpur, Lucknow and Pantnagar improved flexibility.
Lucknow plant commissioned a 2,100 kilolitre rainwater harvesting system; Ambattur plant moved from LPG cooking to electric induction (about 16 tons LPG saved annually).
ESC homologation testing commenced for multiple customers at the ZF Proving Ground; Hemi Anechoic Chamber at ZF Test Track received NABL accreditation.
demand_pricing: Industry CV >6T production grew 8.4% in Q1 FY27; trailer market demand fell about 9% on slower mining, monsoon disruption and higher input costs.
Blue-collar manpower shortage across India in April and May affected industry production.
Aluminium rose from around ₹260/kg to over ₹360/kg per management; about ₹25/kg has come off since July, with easing expected if geopolitical tensions ease.
US and European markets each declined roughly 10% YoY per management, with US declining more; US market now ramping up.
ESC: business nominations secured from three major OEMs; management says ZF will retain majority position in ABS plus ESC market; content per vehicle unchanged across 12V and 24V.
EV bus sales reached 1,417 units in the quarter per management.
risks_watch: Commodity and FX cost pass-through from OEMs: partial recovery so far, balance still under negotiation; margin pressure from aluminium, chemicals and energy costs.
FX volatility: Q1 FY27 carried a ₹1.98 crore FX loss versus a large prior-year FX gain, so reported PAT is sensitive to FX items.
Geopolitical uncertainty affecting US/European export recovery and commodity prices; management declined to quantify export growth for FY27.
ESC ramp: manufacturing starting Q3 of next year, localisation must rise from 40-50% to above 75% by SOP; AEBS/ADAS nominations unconfirmed.
Trailer segment weakness (about 9% market decline) and labour shortages; monsoon-driven volume dip expected in July-September, though early July data looked stronger.
Leadership change: CFO Sweta Agarwal replaced by Rakesh Mishra effective September 1, 2026.
key_quotes: Despite these headwinds, we are at par with the market, supported by improved realizations from new product introductions such as the Exhaust Brake Valve and ECAS variants, along with increased market penetration of our e-compressor solutions.
The Aftermarket business delivered a strong performance in Q1 FY26-27, with sales of ₹158.4 crore, representing a 15.6% year-on-year growth.

Excluding the impact of foreign exchange (FX) gains/losses and one-time items, (₹43.7 crores) Profit before tax stood at ₹140.8 crores in Q1 2026-27, representing a strong 16.9% growth compared to Q1 of the previous financial year.
So we are working on a high level of localization with our local EMS partners where we have possibilities to localize the ECU as well as some of the other products which we are using.
summary.management_tone: Confident on aftermarket, domestic volumes and the ESC pipeline, but cautious on margins and exports, where management repeatedly pointed to commodity inflation, the West Asia conflict and geopolitical uncertainty and declined to give numeric export guidance.
